name: Complete Forbidden pc-Minor Basis for Daisy Cubes
statement: A finite partial cube is a daisy cube if and only if none of its pc-minors is isomorphic to an antipodally punctured hypercube $Q_n^{--}$ with $n\geq3$ or to a graph $O(P,R,A;\mathcal W)$ satisfying the peripheral normal-form hypotheses. Every listed graph is non-daisy and all of its proper pc-minors are daisy cubes.
proof: Daisy cubes are pc-minor-closed. A pc-minimal non-daisy graph either has no peripheral coordinate, in which case it is $Q_n^{--}$, or has a peripheral coordinate, in which case the coordinate normal-form theorem gives $O(P,R,A;\mathcal W)$. The two source theorems also prove that every generated graph is a partial cube, is not daisy, and has only daisy proper elementary pc-minors.
comments: The equivalent intrinsic description deletes a suitably maximal ambient-antipodal pair from a daisy cube with more than one root. The full dimension-free proof remains in the LaTeX paper.
